name: Kadugannawa Ambalama
description: Kadugannawa Ambalama, a charming wooden house converted into an ambalama (lounge) overlooking the Kelaniya Rata River, stands as a serene spot for tourists and locals alike to relax. Constructed in 1847 by a wealthy merchant, it offers a glimpse into colonial architecture and the area's rich history. The building features intricate wood carvings and a traditional roof design, reflecting the craftsmanship of the time. Visitors can enjoy the view while sipping local beverages, making it a popular spot for sightseeing and relaxation in the Kegalle district.

name: Elephant bathing place
description: The Elephant Bathing Place, also known as Abhayagala, is a sacred site in the Kegalle District of Sri Lanka. Historically significant, it was founded by King Mahasena in the 5th century CE, and is noted for its ancient ruins and Buddhist relics. The place is visited by many pilgrims each year, particularly during the full moon poya days. Visitors can explore the temple ruins and soak in the spiritual atmosphere. Nearby, there are also several caves where monks once lived, adding to the area's rich cultural heritage.

name: Algama Water fall
description: Algama Waterfall, nestled in the verdant hills of Kegalle District, Sri Lanka, is a natural marvel offering breathtaking sightseeing opportunities. Known for its tranquil beauty, Algama Waterfall stands as a testament to the country’s natural splendor, drawing in those seeking a moment of peace and serenity.

name: Dunumala ella

name: Millennium Elephant Foundation
description: The Millennium Elephant Foundation, located in the Kegalla district of Sri Lanka, is a non-profit organization dedicated to elephant welfare and conservation. It was established in 2008 by a group of concerned citizens to provide sanctuary for rescued elephants and promote responsible tourism. The foundation offers visitors a unique opportunity to interact with these magnificent creatures while learning about their care and conservation needs. Visitors can see elephants up close at the sanctuary, learn about elephant welfare through educational programs, and participate in volunteer work.

name: rafting no 99
description: Rafting No 99 is an off-the-beaten-path attraction located in Kegalle, Sri Lanka, known for its scenic rafting routes through the region's lush greenery. name: New Regent Spice & Herbal Garden
description: New Regent Spice & Herbal Garden, located in the picturesque district of Kegalle, Sri Lanka, is a unique sightseeing spot where visitors can explore an array of aromatic plants and spices. The garden, established in the early 21st century, showcases various medicinal herbs and spices grown in traditional Sri Lankan methods. It offers a serene retreat for those interested in botany, local culture, and natural remedies. Notable events include guided tours led by knowledgeable staff who share fascinating insights into the plants' uses and historical significance.

name: NewParadise Spice Garden
description: NewParadise Spice Garden, nestled in the picturesque district of Kegalle, Sri Lanka, offers visitors an opportunity to explore the rich biodiversity of spices native to the country. Established as a community project to promote local agriculture and traditional practices, the garden features over 200 species of aromatic plants, each carefully cultivated by local farmers. Visitors can stroll through the serene gardens, learn about the cultural and economic importance of spices in Sri Lankan history, and perhaps even taste some of the fresh herbs and spices. Notable for its role in preserving agricultural heritage, the garden attracts nature enthusiasts and those interested in culinary arts.
